correctness.rationale: For every m,n>=3, the exact normalized three-matching generating function factors as J~(t)(1-t^2/P_J(t)); its 3-by-3 specialization cross-multiplies to Wästlund Eq. (10), and its mean agrees with the known sum over i+j<3. With R=mn/3 the defect h(Rz) has nonnegative coefficients dominated by z^2/[36(1-2z/3)(1-z/2)^2]. The universal a_p satisfies p*a_p<=1/3 for every p>=2 (exact p=2..7 and a decreasing exponential tail). Its logarithmic coefficients c_p=p[z^p](-log(1-h*)) satisfy c_p<=1/2 by a recurrence and the exact mass h*(1)=1/3. A pole-zero pairing shows p[z^p]log J~(Rz)>=1 for every p>=1. Subtracting the defect yields p[z^p]log F(Rz)>=1/2, hence kappa_p >= (p-1)!/(2R^p) >0. Boundary m=n=3 is included and p=1 has stronger margin. No finite enumeration is used for the universal proof. The final packaged checker reproduces 11,500 exact arithmetic assertions.

originality.rationale: Wästlund arXiv:2602.07563v1 explicitly poses all cumulant positivity as Conjecture 10, and proves only a three-edge zero-free disk in Proposition 15. The new point is a uniform ALL-order bound on the negative log-defect coefficients and a positive log-J pairing, which are not consequences of zero-freeness. Alm–Sorkin (2002) supplies transform computations and variance but could not be inspected in full; its priority risk is recorded rather than omitted. published-finding corpus searches for 3-matching/exponential/cumulant aliases returned disjoint combinatorial and Poisson-binomial results. No equivalent or broader covering theorem was identified in accessible full primary literature.

value.rationale: Positivity of all cumulants is a named central conjecture for random optimal matchings, not a generic finite coefficient exercise. The k=3 threshold is the first cardinality at which the rational transform acquires genuinely nonreal zeros, making a sign theorem structurally nontrivial. The result settles every order simultaneously for all rectangular sizes, supplies an explicit nonzero scale, and develops a reusable coefficient-comparison method. The theorem stops at three selected edges and does not overclaim the full conjecture.
